title: 11.5. Query Parameter Naming for Request Parameters
parent_path: 11.5. Query Parameter Naming for Request Parameters

statements.subject: client
statements.description: HTTP methods that do not support request bodies (GET, DELETE) MUST transmit operation request parameters as path parameters or query parameters.
actions: Encode all operation request parameters as path parameters or query parameters when using GET or DELETE HTTP methods

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Query parameter names MUST use camelCase to match the JSON serialization of Protocol Buffer field names.
actions: Format all query parameter names in camelCase corresponding to the JSON serialization of the Protocol Buffer field name

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Repeated Fields: Multiple values MAY be passed by repeating the parameter name (e.g., ?tag=value1&tag=value2) or as comma-separated values (e.g., ?tag=value1,value2)
actions: Pass repeated field values either by repeating the query parameter name or as comma-separated values in a single query parameter

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Nested Objects: Not supported in query parameters; operations requiring nested objects MUST use POST with a request body
actions: Use HTTP POST method with a request body when the operation requires nested object parameters

statements.subject: client
statements.description: All query parameter values MUST be properly URL-encoded per RFC 3986.
actions: Apply RFC 3986 URL encoding to all query parameter values before sending the HTTP request
